title: When the Alibi Burns Again
premise: When the coffin of town founder Auguste Vidal is found empty during a routine exhumation, retired detective Ines Joubert is pulled back into the work he swore off, because the empty grave matches a pattern he's seen before: three 'accidental' deaths that were anything but. Following a coded ledger hidden in the margins of his own bookshop's oldest inventory, Ines uncovers a decades-old scheme in which Vidal faked his death to escape embezzlement charges, leaving a cabal of townspeople bound by silence and blood money. As the anniversary dinner approaches—a ritual the conspirators use to reaffirm their pact—Ines must decide whether exposing the truth will destroy the found family he's built in this town, including police chief Marguerite Osei, who is torn between duty and love for him. In the end, Ines decodes the ledger at the dinner itself, forcing a confession that breaks the pact, but he chooses mercy over prosecution for the coerced, letting only the true architect face justice—and accepting that visibility, and its costs, are the price of belonging.
about_author: Sable Reyes is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent years covering cold cases in coastal Louisiana before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about quiet places where the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet
chapters.summary: Ines Joubert's POV. A slow morning in his failing bookshop establishes his retirement, his routines, and the three unsolved deaths he quietly unraveled years ago. When a city crew arrives to exhume founder Auguste Vidal for a cemetery relocation, Ines feels an old instinct stir. Emotional beat: uneasy calm before disruption.

chapters.title: Empty Hands, Empty Grave
chapters.summary: Ines watches from the crowd as workers lift the lid on nothing but river stones and a rotted shroud. Police Chief Marguerite Osei notices his expression change and asks what he knows; he lies badly. Emotional beat: dread reawakening—the past has teeth again.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She interviews elderly residents about Vidal's death forty years ago and finds their stories suspiciously identical, word for word. She begins to suspect not a cover-up but a covenant. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into isolation—she can trust no witness.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ines discovers faint numeric annotations in the margins of a first-edition inventory book his late wife catalogued—numbers matching dates of the three 'accidents.' He realizes she knew something and died before telling him. Emotional beat: grief reopened as motive.

chapters.title: Accident Number Four
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Felix Arnaud, the cemetery caretaker who reported the empty coffin, found drowned in the retention pond hours after talking to Ines. The town calls it a slip; Ines calls it a message. Emotional beat: guilt and urgency colliding.

chapters.title: Dinner at Eight, Every Year
chapters.summary: Marguerite learns of the Vidal Anniversary Dinner, a closed invitation event attended by the same twelve families for four decades. Her request to attend is politely refused by Mayor Delphine Roux. Emotional beat: institutional walls closing in.

chapters.title: Margins and Marginalia
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. He works the cipher: page numbers paired with ledger figures yield names, amounts, and a recurring phrase—'the glass stays full.' He realizes the code was designed to be readable only by someone who owned the shop. His wife may have been protecting him. Emotional beat: love discovered posthumously.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ines tracks down Camille Vidal, the founder's 'widow,' now ninety-one and sharp as broken glass. She neither confirms nor denies, but slips him a key to a bank box before her nurse ushers him out. Emotional beat: complicity wearing the mask of courtesy.

chapters.title: Box 114
chapters.summary: Marguerite accompanies Ines to the bank, crossing a line professionally. Inside: photographs of the twelve families, a signed pact, and proof Vidal staged his death to flee embezzlement charges—then never left. Someone killed him for real, later. Emotional beat: the mystery deepens into murder.

chapters.title: Twelve Names, Eleven Signatures
chapters.summary: Ines compares the pact against the ledger: one family—the Roux family—never signed. Delphine's father refused, and he was the first 'accident.' The conspiracy wasn't protection; it was enforcement. Emotional beat: righteous anger sharpening into focus.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on Rue Basse
chapters.summary: Someone follows Ines home; his shop window is shattered overnight with a brick wrapped in a page from the ledger. The message is clear: stop. Marguerite insists on staying the night, and the two admit what's growing between them. Emotional beat: tenderness under threat.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Confession
chapters.summary: A dying town archivist, one of the original twelve, tells Ines that Vidal returned secretly in year six to blackmail his own conspirators—and that 'the glass stays full' refers to the toast that seals each year's renewal. Whoever pours the wine holds the power. Emotional beat: revelation with a body count attached.

chapters.title: Who Pours the Wine
chapters.summary: Marguerite pulls forty years of dinner records and finds the same caterer every time: Odile Ferrand, daughter of the family that took over Vidal's shipping fortune. She has poured every glass since her father's death. Emotional beat: suspicion crystallizing on an unlikely figure.

chapters.title: Odile's Version
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She knows Ines is close. Flashbacks reveal her father forced her into the pact as a teenager; she has spent her life pouring poison-laced toasts for those who threatened exposure—including, perhaps, Vidal himself. Emotional beat: sympathy for the devil; survival as inheritance.

chapters.title: An Offer, Politely Made
chapters.summary: Delphine Roux offers Ines the bookshop building free and clear if he leaves town before the anniversary dinner. He declines, quoting his wife's marginal note: 'Some debts are paid in attention.' Emotional beat: temptation refused; identity claimed.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Ines and Marguerite map the dinner venue, an old cannery hall, and plan how to get the ledger decoded pages in front of all twelve families at once. Marguerite risks her badge by going outside official channels. Emotional beat: resolve hardened by love against duty.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Infiltrating as staff, Ines serves the meal himself. As glasses rise for the toast, he reads the first name aloud. Twelve faces go white; Odile stands with the decanter in hand. Emotional beat: held breath—the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Glass Stays Full
chapters.summary: Climax. Odile confesses before the room: her father made her a murderer at seventeen, and every pour since was obedience or self-defense. When Delphine lunges to destroy the ledger, Marguerite intervenes; in the scuffle, the truth spills publicly. Emotional beat: catharsis through confession.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She files reports knowing half the town's founding families belong in handcuffs, then chooses discretion: prosecute Odile's father's crimes posthumously documented, charge the living architect—Delphine—who ordered Felix's drowning. Emotional beat: justice as surgery, not fire.

chapters.title: Sentencing Season
chapters.summary: The trial compresses the town's reckoning. Ines testifies; old friends become strangers; some thank him privately. Odile receives leniency for cooperation and asks him to visit. Emotional beat: the price of survival made visible in a courtroom.

chapters.title: Reopening the Shop
chapters.summary: Ines repairs the window, restocks shelves, and adds a small display: local history, honestly told. Customers return—not for books alone, but because the town finally breathes. Marguerite helps without being asked. Emotional beat: healing as daily practice.

chapters.title: The Last Toast
chapters.summary: One year later, Ines and Marguerite share a quiet dinner in the bookshop. He raises a glass to his wife, to Felix, even to the truth. The ledger goes to the county archive, unsealed. Emotional beat: peace earned—found family, chosen love, survival paid forward.
